# GTM Anatomy — AI infrastructure for go-to-market teams

> GTM Anatomy builds the AI Operating System your go-to-market team runs on, tuned to your business, your brand, and your goals. You own it.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/

---

_AI infrastructure for go-to-market teams_

# Your brand. Your context. Your AI.

Most companies are adding AI to a go-to-market process that was designed before AI existed. We start somewhere else: your foundations, agreed across the team and encoded into an AI Operating System you own, so the work you do once is used every time.

_B2B technology_

_Series A through Series C_

_20 to 200 people_

## What is GTM Anatomy

### AI infrastructure, tuned to your business

Every go-to-market (GTM) team has access to the same models. That is exactly why so much of what they produce sounds the same. Adopting AI without the underlying context is how companies end up with AI-slop: content that sounds like everyone else in the market.

There are no shortcuts. The fundamentals that have always made go-to-market work are still required: messaging, ideal customer profile (ICP) and personas, differentiators, proof points, competitors, and buying signals. Most companies do not have them written down, or sales, marketing, and product each carry a different version of them. AI does not create alignment. It scales whatever you feed it.

We align your team on those foundations, encode them into an AI Operating System tuned to your business, your brand, and your goals, and keep that system learning as the brand evolves. Quite frankly, you are buying something you do not have the time or the expertise to build, and you own it when it is done.

Learn more about GTM Anatomy

**Align the foundations**

One agreed source of truth across sales, marketing, and product, in the words your team actually settled on.

**Encode them once**

Your context lives inside the system, so every output carries your differentiators instead of a model's defaults.

**Keep it learning**

Working files go stale. Your AI Operating System updates the foundations for you and with you as the brand moves.

## Offerings

### Four ways to work with GTM Anatomy

The four offerings run in sequence: diagnose, build, operate, and keep current. Start with the Anatomy Scan, build from the roadmap it produces, then keep the system honest as the business changes. You can stop after any one of them, and everything we build is yours.

### Anatomy Scan

A two-week diagnostic of your go-to-market foundations and your AI readiness. You leave with foundations your team has agreed on, and a sequenced roadmap you can run with or without us.

_Timeline: Two weeks_

### Build Sprint

A focused build against the highest-scoring opportunities on your roadmap. We ship working skills and agents into the systems your team already uses, documented, with the people who will run them trained on them.

_Timeline: Timeline TBC_

### GTM Operating System

The full build. We architect and implement the AI Operating System your go-to-market team runs on, with your context, your standards, and your governance written into it.

_Timeline: Timeline TBC_

### Fractional AI GTM Partner

Ongoing partnership. We keep the system current as the business changes, sequence the audits and update projects, and tell you when and where AI makes sense.

_Timeline: Ongoing_

## The skills library

### Try the method before you hire it

GTM Anatomy publishes a free library of working go-to-market skills for Claude. Same method, same standards, built from real workflows rather than written up as examples. Download one, run it on a real company, and judge the output for yourself.

> Try it yourself. If you would rather have it built for you, talk to us.

## What it means to you

### What this means in your role

The system is the same in every engagement. What it changes depends on what you are measured on.

Good for founders and chief executives who are looking for pipeline from a flat headcount, and AI infrastructure that survives the next model release. You already have the tools. What you do not have is a system.

- One set of go-to-market foundations the whole team works from, agreed and written down.

- Measured where you are measured: pipeline per head, customer acquisition cost (CAC), and go-to-market cost as a percent of new annual recurring revenue (ARR).

- Everything transfers to you at handover: architecture, skills, agents, and runbooks.

Good for revenue leaders who are looking for one operating system the team actually runs, instead of tool sprawl and one-off prompts. You own the outcome, not the architecture, and that is exactly why the architecture has to be someone's job.

- One brand story, carried consistently by sales, marketing, and product.

- A roadmap with sequencing and owners, so the team knows what ships first and why.

- Measured in pipeline created, cycle time, and message consistency.

Good for marketing leaders who are looking for volume without losing differentiation. Everyone has the same models, so the difference has to come from your context.

- Your ICP, personas, messaging, differentiators, and proof points encoded once, then used by everyone every time.

- Brand and answer engine optimization (AEO) audits that show where your owned and earned properties have drifted from the story you are telling now.

- Measured in content throughput per person, and in consistency across every property.

Good for marketing, sales, and revenue operations professionals who are looking for something they can actually operate. You will run what gets built, so it gets documented while it is being built.

- Documented skills, clean integrations, and written runbooks, not a black box.

- Standards for what agents may touch, which data they read, and who approves a change.

- Measured in workflow uptime, data quality, rep adoption, and time to ship a new play.

Good for operating partners and investors who are looking for a repeatable way to raise go-to-market efficiency across a portfolio. The foundations are the same at every company you back, which is what makes the read comparable.

- A current-state read on a portfolio company's go-to-market foundations in two weeks.

- AI spend tied to outcomes, with cost per outcome instrumented from the start rather than reconstructed later.

- Each company owns its own infrastructure, so the value stays with the asset.

### Prefer to book directly?

Pick a time and we will come prepared. Send the company name in advance and we will have read your site before the call.

### Not ready to talk?

# About — GTM Anatomy

> GTM Anatomy aligns go-to-market teams on their foundations, encodes them into an AI Operating System the team owns, and keeps that system learning.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/about.html

---

_About_

# There are no shortcuts.

The fundamentals that have always made a go-to-market (GTM) organization work are still required, at every size and every stage. We align your team on them, then build the AI infrastructure that uses them every day.

## Purpose

### Why GTM Anatomy exists

GTM Anatomy exists to give go-to-market teams AI infrastructure that is tuned to their business, their brand, and their goals.

There are no shortcuts. The information that has always been required for a successful go-to-market team is still required: messaging, ideal customer profile (ICP) and personas, differentiators, proof points, competitors, and buying signals. If that information is not consistent across every person, and now every system, communicating about the business, the brand is not aligned. An unaligned brand loses the three things it cannot afford to lose: authority, credibility, and differentiation.

Adopting AI without that underlying context is exactly how companies end up with AI-slop, content that sounds like everyone else in the market. Differentiate your business in your own context, and the work you do once is used every time your team leverages your AI Operating System.

That is what we build. We align your team on the fundamentals, encode them into your AI Operating System, and keep that system learning as your brand evolves. Quite frankly, you are buying something you do not have the time or the expertise to build. AI is no longer something you try. It is a full-scale implementation, and it has to be done strategically, on a foundation strong enough to keep pace with how fast the technology is moving.

> Do the foundational work once. Use it every time, with confidence.

## The foundations

### The anatomy of a revenue engine

The information that has always been required for a successful go-to-market organization is still required, at every size and every stage. We work through it in this order, because it is a climb and each step depends on the one below it.

1. Ideal customer profile (ICP)

2. Product category

3. Competitors, direct and indirect

4. Personas

5. Messaging

6. Differentiators

7. Proof points

8. Buying signals

9. Data quality

10. Customer relationship management (CRM)

11. Enrichment

12. Outbound process

13. Predictable pipeline

14. Then, and only then: can AI just do it?

Two challenges show up in nearly every company we talk to. They do not have these foundations written down, or they have them and have not agreed on them. Either way, the team is not working from the same source of information, and that is where undifferentiated AI-slop comes from.

The part that is ours is what happens after the alignment. The foundations do not just get agreed once. Your AI Operating System updates them for you and with you. If your brand has moved past the talking points still sitting on your website, we identify what the outside world sees, make the adjustments, and feed them back into the system. Every piece of content from that point forward is attuned to the new brand. The same system feeds audits and update projects, so you know when and where to fix your owned and earned properties, because in today's AI world, inconsistency gets counted against you.

## How we work

### Four things we hold to

**The foundation comes first**

The fundamentals that have always made go-to-market work are still required, at every size and stage. Most companies do not have them, or do not agree on them. We align the team on the foundations before AI touches anything, and we decline briefs that ask us to automate what already exists.

**Your context, not everyone's**

Everyone has the same models. Differentiation comes from your context. We build your AI Operating System from your own material, never a template, so the work you do once is used every time, by everyone on the team.

**A system that keeps learning**

Working files go stale the day after they are written. Your AI Operating System updates the foundations with you, identifies where the outside world has drifted from the brand, and feeds audits and update projects across your owned and earned properties.

**When and where AI makes sense**

Not every task is an AI use case. AI costs are rising and the environmental impact is real. We tell you where AI earns its keep, build it so it is cost-effective at scale, and hand you infrastructure you own and can trust. Part of what you get is someone who will say "this is not a use case for AI."

## Who this is for

### Lean teams expected to punch above their weight

We work with start-ups and scale-ups in B2B technology, roughly Series A through Series C and 20 to 200 people, with a go-to-market function that exists but is under-built for its ambition. The buyer is usually a VP of marketing, a chief revenue officer (CRO), or a founder still carrying go-to-market personally. The shared condition is always the same: a lean team expected to produce like a large one.

Scale here means something specific. Your AI Operating System starts with the go-to-market team and scales across it, then across the rest of the organization, so every function that represents the brand is working from the same context. Scaling across the org is the outcome. Large enterprises are not the customer.

There is a second group we see often: any go-to-market team stuck in ad-hoc AI. Stage matters less than the condition. People using AI like a search engine, foundations missing or unaligned, and output that sounds like everyone else. They usually find us through the free skills library.

### Where we are not a fit

- Pre-product or pre-revenue, with no go-to-market motion to build on.

- Shopping for cheap outbound execution.

- A brief of "just use AI," or "automate what we already do," from a team that will not do the foundational work.

We would rather tell you that in the first call than in the third month.

## Who is behind it

### Founded by Rachel W Bruce

GTM Anatomy was founded by Rachel W Bruce after fifteen years building and leading marketing organizations in cybersecurity, AI, robotics, and technology distribution.

The practice is the method she used to run those teams, rebuilt for what AI can now do. Frameworks over tools, systems over one-offs, and marketing that ties back to revenue and execution or does not get built. The brand speaks as "we" because the work is a system, not a personality.

## Vision + mission

### Where this goes

**Vision**

Go-to-market organizations that are AI-native and aligned: one brand story, one set of talking points, carried consistently by sales, marketing, product, and every AI system that represents the business, across the whole team and, in time, the entire organization.

**Mission**

Give start-ups and scale-ups the confidence to leverage AI to punch above their weight.

Alignment across sales, marketing, and product has always been the priority. AI raises the stakes, because the story is no longer told only by people. It is generated, at volume, by systems. When the context and intelligence behind those systems are tuned to the business, teams execute with confidence and efficiency, and AI-slop is simply not what comes out.

Efficiency without getting bogged down in the build or overwhelmed by the pace of the technology. Ownership of your AI infrastructure, with confidence in what it produces. And a trusted advisor and technology partner who will tell you when and where AI makes sense, and when it does not.

You leave with foundations your team has agreed on and a sequenced roadmap, whether or not you build with us.

# Offerings — GTM Anatomy

> Four ways to work with GTM Anatomy: the Anatomy Scan, a Build Sprint, the GTM Operating System, and a Fractional AI GTM Partner. Everything we build is yours.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/offerings/

---

_Offerings_

# Four ways to work with GTM Anatomy

The offerings run in sequence: diagnose, build, operate, and keep current. Start where you actually are, stop after any one of them, and take everything we build with you.

## The sequence

### Diagnose, build, operate, keep current

Each offering produces the input for the next one. The Anatomy Scan produces a roadmap. A Build Sprint ships the top of that roadmap. The GTM Operating System is the full build with the standards and governance around it. The Fractional AI GTM Partner keeps all of it true as the business changes.

### Anatomy Scan

A two-week diagnostic of your go-to-market (GTM) organization as it actually operates today. We map the current state, align your team on the foundations underneath it, score 15 to 20 opportunities where AI would earn its keep, and hand you a 90-day roadmap. Diagnosis before prescription, and no obligation to build.

_Timeline: Two weeks_

### Build Sprint

A focused build against the highest-scoring opportunities on your roadmap. We build the skills, agents, and workflows from your own material, inside the systems your team already uses, and hand over the runbooks with them. Scoped to a defined set of outcomes, not to an open-ended engagement.

_Timeline: Timeline TBC_

### GTM Operating System

The complete build: the context layer that holds your foundations, the skills and agents your team runs every day, the standards that say what those agents may touch, and the measurement that tells you whether any of it is working. Architected to start with go-to-market and scale across the organization.

_Timeline: Timeline TBC_

### Fractional AI GTM Partner

A standing seat on your go-to-market team. We keep the system current, run the brand and answer engine optimization (AEO) audits that show where your properties have drifted, sequence the update projects, and give you a direct answer whenever the question is whether AI belongs in a given task.

_Timeline: Ongoing_

## Every engagement

### What is true in all four

**Built from your material, never a template**

Your ideal customer profile (ICP), personas, messaging, differentiators, and proof points are the input. If we cannot get them, we align the team on them first.

**Full transfer at handover**

Architecture, skills, agents, runbooks, and written standards. There is no version of this where the system leaves when we do.

**Measurement attached from the start**

Pipeline, cycle time, and cost per outcome, instrumented while we build rather than reconstructed afterwards.

**An honest answer about AI**

Where it earns its keep, and where it does not. Not every task is a use case, and we will tell you which ones are not.

## Investment

### How pricing works

The Anatomy Scan is a fixed engagement. If you go on to build, the Anatomy Scan fee credits into the build. Build Sprint and GTM Operating System engagements are scoped from the roadmap, so the price follows the work rather than a package. The Fractional AI GTM Partner is a monthly commitment.

That is usually the answer to a short call, not to a page. Tell us where the go-to-market team is today and we will tell you where to start.

# Anatomy Scan — GTM Anatomy

> A two-week diagnostic of your go-to-market foundations and AI readiness. You leave with aligned foundations, scored opportunities, and a 90-day roadmap.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/offerings/anatomy-scan.html

---

_Offering 01_

# Anatomy Scan.

A two-week diagnostic of your go-to-market (GTM) foundations and your AI readiness, ending in a roadmap you can run with or without us.

_Two weeks_

_Fixed engagement_

_Fee credits into the build_

## What it is

The Anatomy Scan is a two-week engagement that maps your go-to-market organization as it actually operates today, aligns your team on the foundations underneath it, and scores the opportunities where AI would earn its keep.

It is diagnosis before prescription. We do not build anything during the Scan, and you are not committed to building anything after it. What you own at the end is a picture of the current state that your team agrees with, and a sequence for what to do about it.

## Why it exists

Two challenges show up in nearly every company we talk to. Either the foundations are not written down, or they are written down and sales, marketing, and product each carry a different version.

Both produce the same result once AI is in the workflow: output that is faster, louder, and less differentiated than what came before it. AI does not create alignment. It scales whatever you feed it. The Scan is how we make sure what you feed it is right, and how we find out where AI belongs in your motion before anyone spends money building it.

## What you get

### Inside the engagement

**A current-state map**

Your go-to-market organization as it operates today: team, motion, systems, data quality, and where AI is already in use, including the places nobody has told you about.

**Aligned foundations**

Ideal customer profile (ICP), personas, messaging, differentiators, proof points, competitors, and buying signals, agreed across sales, marketing, and product and written in the words the team settled on.

**15 to 20 scored opportunities**

Ranked by impact, effort, and cost, so the argument for sequencing is on the page rather than in someone's head.

**A 90-day roadmap**

With sequencing, owners, and the measurement attached to each move.

**A written read on when and where AI makes sense**

In your motion specifically, including the places it does not.

**A working session**

We walk your team through all of it, together, because a roadmap nobody has argued with is not aligned.

## Why you need it

You are about to spend real money on AI. The question is not whether the tools work. It is whether the context underneath them is right, and whether the sequence is right.

A roadmap built on foundations your team has actually agreed to is the difference between infrastructure and expensive experimentation. If you go on to build, the Anatomy Scan fee credits into the build. If you do not, the roadmap is still yours, and you can run it with an internal team or another partner.

## Proof points and ROI

### What we hold ourselves to

- Scoped to two weeks, so the decision it informs is not held up for a quarter.

- Every opportunity is scored, so the roadmap is defensible to a board, an operating partner, or a finance review.

- Measurement is attached at the roadmap stage: pipeline, cycle time, and cost per outcome, not added afterwards.

- We decline "automate what we already do" briefs, and we hold the roadmap to the same standard.

<!-- PLACEHOLDER, PENDING CLIENT INPUT Named client outcome or ROI figure from a completed Anatomy Scan. No numbers ship here until a real one is approved. Also pending: a redacted sample Scan document. -->

## Sample

Every Anatomy Scan ends in one document. It opens with the current-state map, moves to the aligned foundations in the words your team agreed on, then the scored opportunity register, then the 90-day roadmap. The last section is the honest one: where AI does not belong in your motion yet, and why.

If you want to see how the thinking works before you commit, the free skills library runs the same method at a smaller scope. Run the Marketing Audit or the Company Identity Builder on your own company and read what comes back.

Try a skill on your own company →

Two weeks to an aligned set of foundations and a roadmap you own. If it is not the right next step, we will tell you what is.

# Build Sprint — GTM Anatomy

> A focused build against the highest-scoring opportunities on your go-to-market roadmap, shipped into your stack and documented so your team can run it.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/offerings/build-sprint.html

---

_Offering 02_

# Build Sprint.

A focused build against the highest-scoring opportunities on your roadmap, shipped into the systems your team already uses and documented so they can run it without us.

_Timeline TBC_

_Scoped from your roadmap_

_Full transfer at handover_

## What it is

A Build Sprint takes the top of your roadmap and ships it.

We build the skills, agents, and workflows against your own context, inside the systems your team already runs, and we hand over the documentation with them. A Sprint is scoped to a defined set of outcomes rather than to an open-ended engagement, which is what makes the cost knowable before it starts.

## Why it exists

Most go-to-market (GTM) teams do not stall on AI because they picked the wrong tool. They stall because nobody owns the build.

The person who could do it already has a full-time job. The prompt that worked brilliantly once lives in someone's notes app and nobody else knows it exists. The roadmap is agreed and then it waits. A Build Sprint puts a defined block of build time against a defined set of outcomes, with your context in it from the first line.

## What you get

### Inside the engagement

**Working skills and agents**

Built from your material, never a template, so the output carries your differentiators and your proof points.

**Integration into your stack**

Inside the systems the team already runs, with clean handoffs between them rather than a parallel process nobody adopts.

**Written runbooks**

How each one is used, what it expects as input, and what good output looks like, so the work survives the person who commissioned it.

**Training for the operators**

A session with the people who will actually run this, not a recording sent to a distribution list.

**A post-sprint review**

What shipped, what it changed, what it cost, and what should come next.

## Why you need it

A roadmap that nobody builds is a document.

The value of the foundations shows up the first time a rep, a marketer, or an operator uses the system and gets output that sounds like your company instead of everyone else's. A Sprint is how you get to that moment in weeks rather than quarters, without hiring for it, and without the person who understands it leaving with the knowledge in their head.

## Proof points and ROI

### What we hold ourselves to

- Built from your own material, so the differentiation is structural rather than editorial.

- Documented at the point of build, which is the only point at which documentation actually gets written.

- Scoped to outcomes, so cost per outcome is knowable before we start rather than after.

- Measured in time to ship a new play, and in throughput per person on the team that runs it.

<!-- PLACEHOLDER, PENDING CLIENT INPUT Named client outcome from a completed Build Sprint. Also pending: the published Sprint duration. -->

## Sample

What ships in a Sprint is a set of working assets, each with a runbook: the skill or agent itself, the context it draws on, the systems it touches, the input it expects, and an example of correct output.

The free skills library is the public version of exactly this work. Every skill there was built the same way, from a real workflow, written down and packaged so someone else can run it. Download one and look at the structure.

See how a skill is built →

If you already have an Anatomy Scan or an equivalent plan, a Sprint is the fastest way to make it real.

# GTM Operating System — GTM Anatomy

> The full build. We architect and implement the AI Operating System your go-to-market team runs on, with your context, standards, and governance written in.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/offerings/gtm-operating-system.html

---

_Offering 03_

# GTM Operating System.

The full build. We architect and implement the AI Operating System your go-to-market team runs on, with your context, your standards, and your governance written into it.

_Timeline TBC_

_Full transfer at handover_

_Architected to scale across the org_

## What it is

The GTM Operating System is the complete build: the context layer that holds your foundations, the skills and agents your team runs every day, the standards that say what those agents may touch, and the measurement that tells you whether any of it is working.

It starts with the go-to-market (GTM) team, because that is where the pressure is, and it is architected to scale across the rest of the organization, so every function that represents the brand is eventually working from the same context. The system we hand over is called your AI Operating System, and it is yours.

## Why it exists

Two years ago, leveraging AI meant opening a browser and experimenting. Today it is a full-scale implementation: infrastructure, context, skills, agents, governance, and cost.

It has to be done strategically, on a foundation strong enough to evolve with the pace of the technology, by people who know when and where AI makes sense and when it does not. Very few go-to-market teams have the time or the in-house expertise to architect that. The ones that try tend to end up with a folder of working files that went stale the day after they were written.

## What you get

### Inside the engagement

**An architecture for your AI infrastructure**

Where context lives, what reads it, how it stays current, and what happens when the model underneath changes.

**Your foundations as the source of truth**

Ideal customer profile (ICP), personas, messaging, differentiators, proof points, and buying signals, encoded once and drawn on by every skill and agent in the system.

**The skills and agents your team runs daily**

Built from your material and integrated into your stack, with runbooks for each.

**Written AI operating standards and governance**

What agents may touch, which data they read, who approves a change, and what the review cadence is. Something finance and security can actually read.

**Measurement, instrumented from the start**

Pipeline, cycle time, and cost per outcome, attached while we build rather than reconstructed at the board meeting.

**Full transfer at handover**

Architecture, skills, agents, runbooks, and standards. You own all of it.

## Why you need it

A lean go-to-market team is expected to produce like a large one. That is only possible if the work you do once is used every time, by everyone, without being re-explained.

That is what an operating system is. The alternative is what most teams have right now: the same models everyone else has, pointed at context nobody has agreed on, producing more of what the market already sounds like, faster. Humans and AI working as one system is bigger than the sum of its parts. Humans and AI working from different versions of the story is just louder.

## Proof points and ROI

### What we hold ourselves to

- Built from your own material, never a template, so the differentiation is structural rather than editorial.

- Standards and governance are written down, so security and finance have something to review rather than a demo to trust.

- Instrumented for cost per outcome, because AI costs are rising and not every task is a use case.

- Everything transfers. There is no version of this where the system leaves when we do.

<!-- PLACEHOLDER, PENDING CLIENT INPUT Named client outcome, adoption figure, or ROI from a completed GTM Operating System build. Also pending: the published build duration. -->

## Sample

The handover contains an architecture document, the context repository holding your foundations, the skill and agent library with a runbook for each, the written operating standards, and the measurement plan.

It is the same shape whether the go-to-market team is six people or sixty. What changes is how many workflows are in it on day one, and how much of the organization it is architected to reach.

The Anatomy Scan sizes this →

The Anatomy Scan sizes the build and the roadmap sequences it. Start there, and the fee credits in.

# Fractional AI GTM Partner — GTM Anatomy

> Ongoing partnership that keeps your AI Operating System current as the business changes, sequences the audits and update projects, and says where AI fits.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/offerings/fractional-ai-gtm-partner.html

---

_Offering 04_

# Fractional AI GTM Partner.

A standing seat on your go-to-market team. We keep the system current as the business changes, sequence the audits and update projects, and tell you when and where AI makes sense.

_Ongoing_

_Cadence TBC_

_Advisor + technology partner_

## What it is

A standing seat on your go-to-market (GTM) team.

We keep your AI Operating System current as the brand, the product, and the market move. We run the audits that show where your owned and earned properties have drifted, sequence the update projects that bring them back in line, and build new skills and agents as the motion changes. What you get is a trusted advisor and technology partner who has sat in the operating chair, not a support queue.

## Why it exists

Working files go stale. So do messaging documents, and so does a system nobody tends.

Brands move faster than their websites. The talking points on your site are usually a version or two behind the story your best rep is already telling. In today's AI world, that inconsistency gets counted against you, because the systems answering questions about your company read your properties, not your intentions.

## What you get

### Inside the engagement

**A recurring working cadence**

With the team that actually runs the system, not a quarterly steering committee.

**Foundations kept current**

When the story changes, the system changes with it, and every output from that point forward is attuned to the new brand.

**Brand and AEO audits**

Answer engine optimization (AEO) audits that show how the outside world, and the AI systems reading it, currently describe you.

**Update projects sequenced by property**

With owners and effort attached, so the backlog is a plan rather than a list.

**New skills and agents as the motion changes**

Built the same way, from your material, documented on delivery.

**A direct answer on AI**

Whenever the question is whether AI belongs in a given task, you get one, including "no."

## Why you need it

The build is the beginning. What determines whether the investment holds is whether somebody is accountable for keeping the context true.

Most go-to-market teams do not have the headcount for that role, and honestly, it is not a full-time job. This is the shape that fits: enough time to keep the system honest, enough distance to tell you the truth about it.

## Proof points and ROI

### What we hold ourselves to

- The system updates the foundations for you and with you, so the context does not decay between projects.

- Audits run against your owned and earned properties, so drift is found by us before it is found by a buyer.

- AI spend stays tied to outcomes, with cost per outcome reviewed on the same cadence as the work.

- Measured in message consistency, time to ship a new play, and spend predictability.

<!-- PLACEHOLDER, PENDING CLIENT INPUT Retained client outcome, tenure, or ROI figure. Also pending: the published working cadence and monthly shape. -->

## Sample

A typical month has a working session with the team, one audit or update project moving, at least one new or revised skill in the system, and a written review of what changed and what it cost. The cadence is set at the start of the engagement and adjusted as the business demands.

How we work →

Whether we built it or you did, the work is the same: keep the context current and keep the spend honest.

# Getting started with Claude skills — GTM Anatomy

> How to use the free GTM Anatomy Claude skills library: browse, download, and drag the file into Claude. Plus the Claude setup guide for teams.

Source: https://gtmanatomy.ai/getting-started.html

---

_The GTM Anatomy skills library_

# Getting Started.

A library of free Claude skills built from real go-to-market workflows. Read how each one works, download the file, run it in Claude. New skills are added regularly.

**Browse**

Head to the Marketing or Sales page to find the skill built for the workflow you are trying to speed up.

**Download**

Each skill is a single, readable Markdown file — what it does, how to prompt it, what you get back.

**Drag Into Claude**

Drop the file into any Claude conversation, or attach it as a project skill. That's the whole install.

Build a system Claude can rely on with repeatable skills, prompts, and more.

## Claude setup guide

### Know before you begin

Three steps to move off ad-hoc prompting and onto a system Claude can rely on.

1. **Separate knowledge from behavior** Static reference material — brand guidelines, personas, messaging docs — is knowledge. Reusable procedures — voice rules, formatting, workflows — are behavior. They belong in different places: knowledge in a Project's Knowledge Base, behavior packaged as a Skill. _Tags: Knowledge Base, Skills._

2. **Choose your layer** Solo builders start with one Claude Project. Teams split knowledge by function and add Skills on top. Enterprises add governance over both — access control, distribution, review cadence. _Tags: Projects, Cowork, Scale._

3. **Scale access deliberately** Start private, expand sharing on purpose, and reach for a live connector — like GitHub — only when a task genuinely needs live repo access. Don't make a connector your default retrieval path for static knowledge; that's where consistency breaks down. _Tags: Governance, Connectors._

### AI 101

The terms you need to know before any of this makes sense.

- **LLM** Short for Large Language Model — the underlying AI system trained on massive amounts of text to understand and generate language. ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok are all products built on top of an LLM.

- **Model** A specific version of an LLM released under a family name — Claude, GPT, Grok — each with its own size, speed, and capability tradeoffs. A graphic comparing models is coming soon.

- **Prompt** A one-off instruction inside a single conversation. Nothing persists once the chat ends.

- **Project** A persistent workspace with a Knowledge Base and custom instructions that every chat inside it can draw on.

- **Skill** A packaged, reusable procedure — like a brand voice guide — that Claude invokes automatically across chat, Code, and Cowork.

- **Cowork** Claude working directly in a local folder of files — structuring documents and running multi-step tasks.

- **Connector / MCP** A live link to an external tool — GitHub, Drive, Slack — that Claude queries in real time. Powerful, but only as stable as the connection itself.

### Best practices

The right setup depends on how many people need the same answer from Claude.

**Solo Builder (Individual)** One Claude Project holding your personal operating brain — who you are, your voice, your clients, your workflows. Loads automatically at the start of every session.

- One Project, one Knowledge Base

- Custom instructions written once

- Optional local CLAUDE.md mirror for Cowork or Code

Read: Turns out Claude needs a brain: https://demandloops.substack.com/p/turns-out-claude-needs-a-brain (source: Kaylee Edmondson, Looped In)

**Small Team (Team)** Split knowledge into focused Projects by function instead of one mega-project, and turn recurring rules into a Skill so every teammate produces on-brand work without re-explaining the style guide.

- Projects split by function, not one mega-project

- Skills for repeatable voice and format rules

- Shared visibility across the team

Read: Claude Cowork + Project: https://ruben.substack.com/p/claude-cowork-project (source: Ruben Hassid, How to AI)

**Org-Wide Rollout (Enterprise)** Same two layers, plus governance — admin-managed groups and roles, org-wide Skill distribution through a private marketplace, and connectors scoped to specific, live-data tasks only.

- Role-based access by group (SCIM-ready)

- Private Skills marketplace for distribution

- Connectors scoped to live-data tasks

Read: Making Claude Cowork ready for enterprise: https://claude.com/blog/cowork-for-enterprise (source: Anthropic)
